security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, documentation links, and reserved example IP ranges. Confirmed issues involve security-impacting IAM examples, including MFA QR output in /tmp and access key creation or deactivation commands. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: MFA QR code is written to a predictable temp path.
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-owned temporary file with restrictive permissions, delete it after enrollment, and warn users before creating MFA devices.

remediation.issue: Access key rotation examples can create or deactivate live credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval, add dry-run alternatives, and avoid storing generated secrets in shell variables or logs.

remediation.issue: The time-based EC2 policy example grants broad access.
remediation.suggestion: Replace ec2:* and Resource * with specific actions and resources, or label the template as a temporary exception.

content.value_statement: IAM permissions often drift into risky access patterns. This skill guides policy review, MFA checks, access key hygiene, and least privilege remediation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies IAM policies with wildcard actions and inline user policies.
Checks for IAM users without MFA and reviews MFA enforcement patterns.
Finds access keys older than 90 days and outlines rotation steps.
Reviews unused roles and trust relationships with external accounts.
Provides IAM policy templates for S3, MFA, time, and IP conditions.
Includes a Python report script for MFA, old keys, and broad policies.
limitations: Requires AWS credentials and IAM permissions before AWS CLI examples can run.
Does not replace AWS IAM Access Analyzer or formal cloud security review.
Some examples modify IAM resources and need explicit approval before use.
Policy templates must be adapted and tested before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Quarterly IAM Review
use_cases.description: Audit users, policies, roles, and access keys before a scheduled security review.

use_cases.title: Least Privilege Cleanup
use_cases.description: Replace broad permissions with scoped policy statements for application teams.

use_cases.title: Cloud Hardening Plan
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized IAM hardening checklist for an AWS account or environment.

prompt_templates.title: Review IAM Risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an AWS account or exported IAM notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my IAM setup for risky users, policies, roles, and access keys. Summarize the highest priority fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Find MFA Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused check for missing multi-factor authentication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me identify IAM users without MFA and recommend a safe rollout plan for enforcement policies.

prompt_templates.title: Create Least Privilege Policy
prompt_templates.scenario: Policy design for a scoped application need.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a least privilege IAM policy for this workload. Explain each permission and list assumptions that need validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Automated Hardening
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for repeatable IAM audits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an IAM hardening workflow that checks MFA, old access keys, wildcard permissions, unused roles, and external trust relationships.

output_examples.input: Review these IAM policies for least privilege problems.
output: Flags wildcard actions as high priority review items.
Separates read-only findings from changes that need approval.
Recommends narrower actions, scoped resources, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Generate an IAM hardening report for my account.
output: Summarizes users without MFA, old access keys, unused roles, and broad policies.
Ranks fixes by risk and operational impact.
Includes a checklist for remediation tracking.

output_examples.input: Create safer S3 access for each user.
output: Proposes user-scoped object access and limited bucket listing.
Explains required conditions and naming assumptions.
Calls out tests to run before deployment.

best_practices: Run discovery commands with read-only credentials before making IAM changes.
Test every generated policy in a non-production account or policy simulator.
Document assumptions, resource scope, and approval status for each change.
anti_patterns: Applying generated IAM policies directly to production without review.
Keeping long-term access keys active after role-based access is available.
Using wildcard actions or resources when specific permissions are known.

faq.question: Does this skill run AWS commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any command that changes IAM resources should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can it replace IAM Access Analyzer?
faq.answer: No. It complements AWS tools by organizing review steps and explaining least privilege remediation.

faq.question: What AWS permissions are needed?
faq.answer: Read-only IAM permissions support most reviews. Key rotation or MFA device creation requires additional administrative permissions.

faq.question: Can it help write new IAM policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft scoped policy guidance, explain permissions, and list validation steps before deployment.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production accounts?
faq.answer: Yes, for review workflows. Production changes need approvals, testing, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is described for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
